extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, journalists and researchers interested in the Killian documents controversy, media ethics, and standards for handling documentary evidence in reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for journalists producing news segments that rely on disputed documentary evidence — i.e., how to authenticate documents, vet sources, avoid conflicts of interest, and handle follow-up reporting when questions arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Must obtain clear authentication of any of the Killian documents from any document examiner; proof of authenticity is the only acceptable journalistic standard to justify using them in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because CBS had only faxed and photocopied duplicates, authentication to professional standards was impossible; original documents are required for generally recognized document-expert authentication. The Panel found the failure to obtain clear authentication to be one of the most serious defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate representation of expert findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not falsely state that an expert authenticated documents when the expert only supported a narrower point (e.g., authenticated a signature or noted documents were 'from the same source').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel criticized CBS for the false statement that an expert had authenticated the Killian documents when all he had done was authenticate one signature from one document; reporting must precisely convey the scope and limits of expert opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize source background
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly investigate and disclose the publicly available and potentially controversial background of the source who provided the documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel faulted CBS for failing to scrutinize Bill Burkett's background; vetting a source's credibility, motives and public history is essential before relying on documents they provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish chain of custody / provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Locate and interview the person understood to be the source of the documents and establish the chain of custody for the materials used in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel cited failure to find and interview Burkett's source and thus failure to establish provenance; establishing who created, possessed, and transmitted documents is necessary to assess authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate claims about document origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assert that documents 'were taken from [an individual's] personal files' without a factual basis for that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel identified the failure to establish a basis for the Segment's statement that the documents 'were taken from Colonel Killian’s personal files' as a serious defect — such provenance claims require corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop adequate corroboration and cross-check with official records
rubrics_metrics.description: Support statements in documents with corroborating evidence and carefully compare disputed documents to official records to identify inconsistencies in content and format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel found CBS failed to develop adequate corroboration or compare the memos to TexANG records; routine cross-checks against archival or official sources can reveal content or format anomalies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview a range of knowledgeable witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview multiple former colleagues or others with differing perspectives who served with the individuals implicated by the documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel criticized CBS for not interviewing a range of former National Guardsmen who served with Killian and might have offered different perspectives; diverse sourcing prevents overreliance on a single viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating misleading impressions via selective presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not present interviews or soundbites in a way that creates the impression a source authenticated content when they lacked personal knowledge or were asked to assume accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: introducing Robert Strong as 'standing by his judgment that the documents are real' when he had only briefly seen copies and was told to assume they were accurate. Disclaimers and context must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a vetting process matched to speed, significance and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain vetting procedures capable of handling the production speed, significance and sensitivity of fast-moving, high-stakes segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel found CBS lacked a vetting process adequate for the fast production and importance of the Segment; organizations should adopt procedures that scale to the story's potential impact and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest and the appearance of political coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid contact or arrangements with political campaign officials that could create the appearance of assisting a campaign rather than reporting, and prevent conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel faulted a producer's pre-air call to a Kerry campaign official as a clear conflict of interest that created the appearance of political bias; journalists must avoid such contacts or disclose them and manage conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not stridently defend reporting without re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: When substantive challenges arise, do not reflexively defend the report; instead, probe the questions raised and reassess the evidence objectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel criticized CBS's 'strident defense' of the Segment without adequately probing criticism; follow-up coverage should investigate challenges rather than simply defending the original report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use independent oversight and avoid reusing the same personnel to defend contested work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not have many of the same individuals who produced and vetted a controversial segment produce the follow-up reports defending it; use independent reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel noted allowing the same personnel to produce defense coverage compounded the problem; independent review helps ensure impartiality and credibility in aftermath reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue accurate public statements about sources and expert vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure press statements accurately reflect the reliability of sources and what experts actually opined about document authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel condemned inaccurate CBS press statements claiming the source was 'unimpeachable' and that experts had vouched for authenticity; public communications must be precise and not overstate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select document examiners by qualification, not by likely endorsing position (avoid expert-shopping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and consult the best-qualified document examiners regardless of whether their likely conclusions support the desired narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel criticized efforts to find examiners who would vouch for authenticity rather than the best available examiners; selection should be merit-based and comprehensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid preparing coverage designed to support a pre-existing segment
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent reporting should not be crafted primarily to bolster the original segment rather than to provide accurate, balanced coverage of newly raised issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel found CBS prepared stories that sought to support the Segment instead of offering balanced coverage of the controversy; follow-up must prioritize accuracy over defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve originals to enable professional forensic examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain original documents and avoid destroying originals, since copies (faxes/photocopies) may preclude definitive forensic authentication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provider's alleged burning of originals and CBS's use of faxed/photocopied duplicates made professional authentication impossible; procedures should require preservation of originals and chain-of-custody documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent experts' credentials and the limits of their analyses correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish among types of experts (handwriting analyst, forensic document examiner, typewriter/typography expert) and accurately state what each did and did not conclude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBS misrepresented the roles and conclusions of its consultants (e.g., conflating signature comparison with full document authentication); reporting must clearly communicate the nature and limits of expert analyses.
